directions.name: I — Crayon discoveries
directions.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE original landscape illustration direction board for Hey Kahani, a playful thoughtful children's storytelling brand. This is an exploratory art study for website assets. No typography, text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, brand marks, product hardware or photographic website mockups. Do not repeat the earlier kite/book/sun/leaf 6-icon grid or cream footer strip. Invent original art, no copyrighted characters. Brand colour anchors: Gulab Red #D3000A, Kesar Sand #FFF1D6, Sky Blue #63C3FE, Mango Yellow #FECB74, Story Ink #05334A. Support with Parrot Green #2B9863, Marigold Orange #FF5D27, Lavender tea #D6C9E4, sparse Hibiscus Pink #EF2289. Not every colour needs to appear. Keep each board internally coherent, genuinely distinct in medium and construction. Explore freely rather than treating earlier questionnaire preferences as hard limits. The attached references from the conversation are general inspiration only. MEDIUM: exuberant wax-crayon and oil-pastel drawing, strongly tactile dry broken wax strokes with irregular pressure, visible overlapping marks and deliberate wonky childlike proportions, expertly composed. NO clean vector contours, smooth digital blobs or polished clipart. Warm white paper with no strong yellow wash. Build an airy specimen board of 5 different little worlds: a red toy train with wildly mismatched wonky wheels and a sky-blue crayon cloud of steam; a yellow raincoat and blue boots splashing in a scribbled puddle; an orange cat asleep curled on a green cushion; a crooked blue telescope pointing at three loosely scribbled stars; and a tiny red spinning top with curved motion marks. Big confident scribbled fills, uncoloured gaps in pigment, nervous energetic lines and occasional overdrawing. Objects feel honestly drawn by hand but designed with taste; simple small eyes only on cat. Compose variable scales, generous blank paper, no rigid grid, no extra confetti. This should feel warm raw spontaneous and visibly unlike a digital vector set.

MEDIUM: bold two-colour risograph print illustration, printed ONLY Gulab-red ink and Monsoon Blue #2578B7 on Kesar-cream stock, with dark ink overlap where the two inks cross. Strong visible riso halftone screens, slight off-register edges, flat graphic stamp-like shapes but much bolder poster composition than small friendly icons. No other hues. Landscape art board divided into THREE UNEQUAL illustrative panels with broad cream gutters and no text. Large left panel: a blue bicycle with red woven basket full of wildly oversized leaves and one little red bird sitting on handlebar. Upper right: two mismatched red/blue socks hanging on a curling line, rhythmic patterned shadow shapes behind. Lower right: a red teapot sending a blue steam ribbon that turns into a loose constellation. Punchy woodcut-like silhouette, large halftone dot fields in selected shadows, high contrast, witty unexpected proportion, charming imperfect registration. Enough cream negative space that art remains website-friendly. No faux letters or printed captions. Clearly a limited-ink graphic print system, not watercolour, not paper craft or clean clipart.

MEDIUM: continuous-line modern illustration with gestural thin Story Ink monoline strokes that weave and loop, extremely spare, elegant playful negative space. Each object should appear constructed from one confident uninterrupted curling line, with just one or two offset small geometric colour planes behind it. Very airy white background. Across the landscape board arrange four large original vignettes at varying heights: a long-necked giraffe bending down to inspect a tiny red ball, a bent desk lamp illuminating a yellow irregular oval of light, a watering can whose flowing line becomes a blue winding river, and a pair of oversized headphones whose cable becomes a little looping house. One or two small dashed motion traces allowed. Restrict colour patches to sky blue, Gulab red, Mango yellow and cream; outline does most of the work. Fine intentional paths, offbeat perspective, visual wit, thoughtful balance. In contrast to naïve doodles, this should feel disciplined continuous-line drawing with minimal marks and abundant blank space.

Dense matte wool loops, simple embroidered running stitches, broad hand-cut felt silhouettes, slight real material depth and soft contact shadows on warm white felt ground. Children's illustration with modern graphic discipline, not photoreal product photography. Create FIVE isolated motifs in a loose roomy arrangement: a round striped felt snail with spiralled couched-yarn shell; a yellow crescent hugging one small red embroidered star; a blue rain cloud with 3 thick dangling yarn raindrops; an oversized green leaf with red stitched vein; and an orange mushroom with chunky cream tufted spots. A tiny simple eye can appear on the snail only; everything else faceless. Large simplified shapes and big visible stitches, crisp but irregular cut edges, red blue yellow anchors, supporting green and orange, very restrained clutter. Show the genuine difference in material of flat felt and coiled thread. No sewn-on label text, no knitted words, no beige boho rainbow aesthetics. Bright warm playful touchable motifs.

MEDIUM: playful editorial cartoon drawing with bold, variable-width brush-ink outlines, angular lively silhouettes, exaggerated gestures, graphic flat colour and occasional crosshatching.
